Subject: Renewal pricing for CloudHam - expansion and co-term?

Hi Neha —

We’re starting the renewal conversation for CloudHam (contract ends 2027-06-30). Since we’ve seen steady growth, we want to add an extra 60 GPU-hours/month mid-contract starting Apr 1 to support a new diagnostics feature. Can you share renewal pricing that: (1) co-terms the new 60 GPU-hours with our existing June renewal date, and (2) outlines any uplift discounts or credits for mid-contract growth?

Procurement (cc'd) wants to understand overall unit economics and any one-time credits you can apply to smooth the transition. We prioritize predictable unit cost; any guidance on tiered discounts as we scale would be helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on quick call if useful.

— Elise

CloudHam Health

Elise —

Thanks for the context and congrats on the new diagnostics rollout. I’ve sketched a short proposal (attached) that balances predictable per-GPU pricing with credits to offset the mid-term uplift. Key points up front:

- Co-term: We can co-term the added 60 GPU-hours so all capacity aligns to your 2027-06-30 renewal. No pro-rata on per-hour price — we normalize to the June renewal date.
- Tiered pricing: New combined commitment tiers with stepped discounts at 1.25x and 1.5x current commit. Example table included in sheet.
- One-time onboarding credit: $18,000 in usage credits applied across Apr–Jun to cover migration/testing spikes.
- Volume uplift credit: For any committed increase >30% inside the renewal window, we add a one-time 5% bill credit (applied at next invoice).
- Doc/PO: Attached renewal proposal PDF and an editable co-term worksheet (xls) for your procurement team.

If procurement prefers a lower upfront credit and a deeper per-unit discount instead, we can trade the onboarding credit for incremental discount points — I outlined two swap scenarios on page 2.

Suggested next steps: 1) quick sync with Procurement to confirm swap preference, 2) finalize PO language and sign DocuSign. I can loop Legal for the co-term amendment once you approve economics.

I’ll also put Karthik on thread to confirm SLA/throughput guarantees for the additional capacity.

Best,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement looked through the sheet and had two asks:

1) Can you move some of the $18k onboarding credit into a one-off invoice credit we can book this quarter instead of usage credits spread over months? Our finance team prefers invoice-level credits.
2) The 5% volume uplift credit is helpful — can that be increased to 7% if we commit to a 1.4x uplift (vs the 1.25x example)? We’re willing to sign up to the 1.4x level if the incremental incentive is stronger.

We also need to confirm: if we add the 60 GPU-hours now, does it displace any reserved capacity for other customers during burst periods? SLA clarity there will help us justify the spend to leadership.

Jamal/Elise —

Thanks for the detailed asks — happy to accommodate both with a small restructure. Summary of final offer below (I’ll send an updated PDF/DocuSign link once you confirm):

1) Credit structure: Convert $18,000 onboarding usage credit -> $18,000 invoice credit applied to your May invoice (one-line credit). This should satisfy your finance booking requirement.

2) Volume uplift: If you commit to a 1.4x increase to your committed GPU-hours now (effective Apr 1, co-term to 2027-06-30), we’ll increase the volume uplift credit to 7% (one-time bill credit applied to the July invoice after renewal). If you land between 1.25x–1.4x, we’ll prorate between 5%–7%.

3) SLA & capacity isolation: The added capacity will be placed in your Dedicated pool with the same throughput SLOs; it won’t be used for public burst capacity. During rare regional capacity events we have fallback options (compatible quantized model variant or cross-region failover). Karthik will confirm the SLO language below and will be copied into the amendment.

4) Trade option: Alternatively, we can replace the invoice credit with an additional 2% off per-unit rate (per-hour) for Apr–Jun if you prefer lower invoice amounts vs credits. We left both options in the worksheet.

Next steps: 1) Confirm whether you prefer the invoice credit or deeper per-unit discount; 2) confirm 1.4x commitment band; 3) I’ll issue updated DocuSign and PO guidance (we can accept a signed PO against the amendment).

Karthik — can you add the SLA blurb to the amendment and confirm throughput targets we’ve offered (p99 latency under 150ms for 512-token responses, 95% availability for dedicated pool)?

Thanks — I can jump on a 20-min call if helpful.
